title: Positioning experiments: vertical hypotheses and battle rhythms
content:
Purpose:
Rapidly test differentiated messaging across five verticals (Fintech, Healthcare, Legal, Enterprise SaaS, Gov/Defense) to validate the hypothesis that an inference-first value prop (cost predictability + reliability + private deployment options) converts better than model-access-first messaging for mid-market and enterprise buyers.

High-level experiment design:
- Run 6 week micro-campaigns per vertical with 3 message variants each: (A) Cost & throughput economics, (B) Reliability & fallbacks (SLO-first), (C) Compliance & private deployment.
- Channels: outbound SDR sequences, demo scripts, 1-pagers for AE, two technical blog drafts, one short case-study shadow test.
- Metrics to track: MQL->SQL conversion lift by message, demo-to-poc rate, time-to-contract, objections logged, technical deep-dive requests, feature asks.

Guiding hypotheses (one-liners):
- Fintech: "Predictable inference economics beats model novelty when regulators and cost-per-transaction matter."
- Healthcare: "Private deployments + auditability win before model fidelity for internal clinical workflows."
- Legal: "Chain-of-custody and reproducible outputs are mandatory — show audit trails and fallbacks."
- Enterprise SaaS: "Integrations + per-route observability shorten procurement cycles more than marginal quality wins."
- Gov/Defense: "Network isolation and certified key management unlock procurement; advertising latency SLAs feels secondary."

Fintech notes (nuanced):
- ICP: payments orchestration platforms, risk/decisioning teams, fraud scoring, transaction enrichment services (MAUs 100k+).
- Primary pain: erratic inference cost on bursty transaction volumes; black-box fallbacks to public endpoints; audit/regulatory proof.
- Core proof points to use: per-token cost banding across commit tiers, deterministic autoscaling policies (burst vs reserve), throughput SLAs, KV-cache benefit for repeated patterns in transaction stream.
- Competitor angle: position vs. vendors that emphasize model leaderboard accuracy (OpenAI-style) — our counter is production economics and predictable unit cost with consistent latency.
- Objections to preempt: "We already use cloud ML endpoints" -> show total cost of ownership math and sample invoice comparisons; "We need bespoke models" -> show model pinning + rollout controls.
- Quick win collateral: 1-page 'Cost-of-inference' calculator + short demo showing 99th percentile latency with fallback to lower-cost model variant.

Healthcare notes (nuanced):
- ICP: EHR vendors, clinical decision support, telehealth platforms, enterprise health systems.
- Primary pain: data residency, PHI handling, auditability for clinical decisions, regression risk on model updates.
- Core proof points: Private deployment blueprint (VPC + KMS + audit logs), eval harness tied to clinical prompt sets, rollback/rollback policies, canarying by patient cohort.
- Compliance messaging: HIPAA alignment (not a legal claim) — focus on controls customers can own. Highlight on-prem option for air-gapped regulators.
- Competitive tilt: against hosted-first vendors, emphasize that Dedicated + Private pattern avoids data egress and gives legal teams control.

Legal notes (nuanced):
- ICP: eDiscovery platforms, contract lifecycle management, law firm tech teams.
- Pain: explainability, deterministic outputs for evidentiary purposes, long-term retention of model outputs with provenance.
- Messaging play: audit trail + reproducible-run IDs + function calling with strict schema enforcement. Provide sample chain-of-custody demo where a document transformation is replayable.
- Closing proof points: retention policies, cryptographic checksums, signer metadata in outputs.

Enterprise SaaS notes (nuanced):
- ICP: product teams adding AI features (search, summarization, helpdesk), platform teams standardizing infra for internal apps.
- Pain: unpredictable latency for interactive UX, inability to control unit economics as usage scales, fragmented observability across endpoints.
- Messaging: "Same API across hosted, dedicated, private" — value: lower integration cost; per-route cost analytics for product managers; rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic fallback).
- Sales enablement: demo script that toggles a per-route setting to show immediate cost/latency impact, example dashboard screenshot showing token-level cost.

Gov/Defense notes (nuanced):
- ICP: agency modernization teams, classified program integrators, defense primes (non-IT buyers often with compliance managers).
- Pain: procurement with C&A constraints, need for hardware isolation, FIPS/KMS demands, manual audits, long procurement cycles.
- Messaging: emphasize private control plane, on-prem validated package, HSM/KMS integration, long-term support contracts, and evidence of hardened runtime (kernel selection and attestation story).
- Tactical: create a short 'accreditation checklist' for technical reviewers.

Cross-vertical common threads to test:
- Message A (Economics framed): sample opener: "Cut inference unit costs by 40% for heavy-production use cases without sacrificing latency guarantees."
- Message B (Resilience framed): sample opener: "Keep critical LLM features online with automated fallbacks and SLA-backed capacity."
- Message C (Control framed): sample opener: "Run private inference with audit-ready outputs and customer-managed keys."

Experiment logistics and playbook items:
- SDR templates: 3 variants per vertical, short subject lines, one technical hook line + one biz outcome line.
- AE kit: 2-minute demo script, 1-page pricing comparator, 1-page security primer.
- SE kit: reproducible demo repo link (internal), checklist for on-site/private POCs, and eval dataset recipes.
- Content: blog outline per vertical (problem, why model access alone is insufficient, how 'serving' wins).
- Measurement: capture objection tags in CRM, tag each contact by message variant, weekly review with product to capture feature asks.

Risks & unknowns to surface to PM/Prod: 
- H1: Customers may conflate "dedicated" with "expensive" — need clear cost models and case studies.
- H2: Gov/Defense procurement timing could skew metrics — treat these separately and use surrogate metrics (RFI progression).
- H3: Messaging that emphasizes private deployments may reduce inbound velocity from small companies who prefer hosted simplicity — expect different funnels.

Next actions (2-week sprint):
1) Lock SDR templates + AE kit (owner: Marco Li)
2) Build quick 'cost comparator' sheet and embed sample numbers (owner: Sofia Nguyen)
3) Draft two short technical blog posts (owner: Ethan Romero)
4) Instrument CRM tagging for message variant (owner: Aisha Patel)

Open questions for leadership: 
- Do we want to publicize a specific SLA target in outbound messaging or keep it discovery-only?
- Which partner stories (if any) are safe to use as early case studies for private deployments?
- Budget: allocation for paid outreach per vertical (recommended starting point: modest for Fintech + Enterprise SaaS, symbolic for Gov/Defense).

Appendix: sample SDR subject lines and first lines (pick one per variant):
- Fintech/Economics: Subject: "Lower inference costs for high-volume transactions" / First: "Hi <name>, I ran a quick cost model for payments pipelines — can I share a 2-min breakdown?"
- Healthcare/Control: Subject: "Run clinical models inside your VPC (PHI-friendly)" / First: "Hi <name>, we helped an EHR partner move inference on-prem with audit logs — curious how you handle PHI today?"
- Legal/Traceability: Subject: "Replayable LLM runs for legal workflows" / First: "Hi <name>, curious if reproducible outputs are a blocker for your eDiscovery pipeline?"

Notes on competitive positioning language to avoid (branding safe list):
- Avoid calling out competitors by name in marketing collateral unless cleared by comms; internal sales can use competitive battlecards.
- Use comparative language focused on customer outcomes rather than direct feature name-calling.

Document version notes:
- This is an experiment brief — iterate rapidly. Expect lots of shorthand and change. We'll promote to a formal vertical playbook if any message variant lifts conversion by +15% at the SQL stage.

End of brief.
